newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka ruling coalition set to win local polls.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka ruling coalition set to win local polls.

text.p: Sri Lanka's ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition looked set for a sweeping victory in local polls on Saturday, its first political test since winning power in 1994.
The PA had won 136 of 168 councils where official results were declared by 11 a.m (0500 GMT) and was leading in most others where counting was still continuing, the Elections Department said.
The main opposition United National Party (UNP) won the remaining 32 councils where results were announced.
Final results were expected later on Saturday, it said.

Sri Lankans voted on Friday in local polls marred by violence to elect 3,567 representatives to 238 municipal, urban and other smaller bodies, in what is widely seen as a mid-term appraisal of President Chandrika Kumaratunga's government.
Political sources said while the PA had improved its position in the island's rural areas it was mostly rejected by voters in the urban centres, including capital Colombo.
"The minority vote in Colombo seems to have swung the UNP's way. We expected a different outcome in Colombo," goverment minister A.H.M. Fowzie, PA's campaign manager for Colombo, told Reuters.
The PA also lost the municipal council in the minority Tamil dominated central hill country of Nuwara Eliya and northcentral Kurunegala to UNP.
But it wrestled two councils, in southern Galle and Sri Jayewardenepura-Kotte, a Colombo suburb, from the UNP.
"On the basis of results already out, the PA is winning a comfortable victory," said senior UNP lawmaker Karunasena Kodituwakku.
"However, there have been many complaints of violations, such as intimidation of our supporters and casting of illegal votes. We hope to pursue these cases later," he told Reuters.
The Elections Department said 65 percent of some 10 million eligible voters had cast ballots in the election, up from 61 percent in the previous 1991 local polls.
It said voter turnout was moderate early on Friday but had picked up later in the day.

The department said the PA had garnered 52 percent of votes in areas where results were declared, lower than the overall 62 percent it polled in the 1994 presidential elections, which Kumaratunga won.

State television said a precautionary overnight curfew imposed on the capital Colombo and elsewhere was being extended until 1 p.m. (0700 GMT) to curtail post-election violence. It was originally to be lifted at 8 a.m. (0200 GMT).
Police would decide later whether to further extend the curfew, the state television said.
Police said the situation was peaceful in Colombo and surrounding areas and there were no reports of violence since the curfew was imposed late on Friday.
